ee_text: Represent and interpret data on a picture or bar graph, given a model and a graph to complete.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create a line plot with accurate spacing and labels, including a title and axis labels. I can use the line plot to compare the lengths of different groups of specimens (e.g., comparing males and females). I can calculate the average length of the specimens and explain how I found it using the line plot. I can create a line plot to represent data collected from a real-world situation, such as measuring the heights of plants in a garden. I can use the line plot to draw conclusions about the data, such as which plant grew the tallest or which height range had the most plants.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create a line plot with accurate spacing between the marks on the number line, ensuring each fraction is represented correctly. I can use the line plot to find the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in a data set. I can explain my reasoning for finding the difference in length using the line plot.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can create a line plot with appropriate spacing between the marks on the number line. I can identify the most frequent measurement and the least frequent measurement from the line plot.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can draw a line plot with uneven spacing between the marks on the number line. I can identify individual data points on the line plot but struggle to compare them.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can interpret data from a variety of graphs to answer questions. I can Answer questions based on information provided in a picture schedule. I can Tell how many sunny days there were in a month, based on a weather graph.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can demonstrate awareness that symbols may be used to represent objects and events. I can Picture of ice cream represents a favorite flavor. I can Picture of snow represents a snowy day.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can make observational statements about data in a picture and bar graph. I can Tell you what they observe on a graph of students’ eye colors. I can Show students a graph of the Big 12 football teams and ask them what they think it is about.

source: CCEE Math Standards 2024 V1 Complete.xlsx (school)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.
text: Recognize angles as geometric shapes that are formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement: a. An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays, by considering the fraction of the circular arc between the points where the two rays intersect the circle. An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a "one-degree angle" and can be used to measure angles. b. An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.
ee_text: Recognize angles in geometric shapes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain the relationship between angles and circles, including the concept of arc length and central angles. I can use angle measures to solve problems in real-world situations, such as calculating the height of a building or the distance to a star. I can explain how angles are used in different fields, such as engineering, architecture, and astronomy.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that an angle is formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint. I can measure angles by imagining a circle with its center at the endpoint and measuring the fraction of the circle's arc between the rays. I can recognize that a one-degree angle is formed by turning 1/360 of the way around a circle. I can use degrees to measure the size of any angle.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify angles in different shapes and objects. I can compare the sizes of angles by looking at how wide they are.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify angles as pointy shapes made by two lines meeting at a corner.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can recognize angles in geometric shapes. I can draw an arc to identify the angles after teacher draws a geometric shape on a whiteboard. I can when given pictures of different geometric shapes and angles that match the shapes, overlay shapes with matching angles.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can identify shapes that contain angles. I can when given a square and a circle, identify the square. I can find an object that is shaped like a square in the classroom.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can identify an angle. I can wipe away the shape that does not contain an angle when teacher draws a shape with an angle and a circle. I can identify as many angles as they can see or feel on the playground. I can when given an angle template, hold it to shapes in the classroom and tell if it matches. I can when given a set of four shapes (one with angles and three with no angles), indicate the shape with angles.

source: CCEE Math Standards 2024 V1 Complete.xlsx (school)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.
text: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.
ee_text: Compare angles as larger than, smaller than, or the same size as another angle.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a protractor to measure angles to the nearest half-degree. I can sketch angles of specified measure accurately, without using a protractor. I can use my knowledge of angles to solve real-world problems, such as designing a ramp for a toy car or building a birdhouse.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a protractor to measure angles accurately to the nearest degree. I can sketch angles of specified measure accurately, using a protractor to check my work.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a protractor to measure some angles, but I sometimes have trouble reading the markings accurately. I can sketch angles of specified measure, but my sketches are often not very accurate.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify angles as "big" or "small" but cannot use a protractor to measure them. I can draw lines that are supposed to be angles but do not use a protractor to measure them.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify angles as larger and smaller. I can when given an angle shaded to less than 45⁰ and one shaded to more than 120⁰, indicate “Which is larger?” I can when given two fraction puzzles pieces, one containing a significantly larger angle than the other, indicate “Which is smaller?”
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can replicate an angle. I can use popsicle sticks to replicate a given angle. I can Bend a pipe cleaner to replicate a given angle.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can differentiate angles in shapes. I can when given an angle and a circle, indicates “Which is an angle?” I can when given a ball and a cube, indicate “Which has an angle?”

source: CCEE Math Standards 2024 V1 Complete.xlsx (school)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles.
text: Recognize angle measure as additive. When an angle is decomposed into non-overlapping parts, the angle measure of the whole is the sum of the angle measures of the parts. Solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the problems, e.g., by using an equation with a symbol for the unknown angle measure.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.4.G.2.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why the angle measure of a whole is the sum of the angle measures of its parts. I can use my understanding of angle measures to solve complex problems, such as finding the missing angle in a polygon or designing a structure with specific angle measurements. I can apply my knowledge of angle measures to real-world situations, such as designing a ramp for a wheelchair or calculating the angle of a satellite dish to receive a signal.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can decompose an angle into two non-overlapping parts and find the sum of their measures. I can use an equation with a variable to represent the unknown angle measure in an addition or subtraction problem involving angles. I can solve real-world and mathematical problems involving angles by adding or subtracting their measures.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare the size of two angles and tell which is bigger or smaller. I can combine two angles and estimate the total angle measure.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify angles in shapes and real-world objects. I can estimate the size of angles.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.4.G.2.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Draw and identify lines and angles and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
text: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
ee_text: Recognize parallel lines and intersecting lines.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can draw and identify different types of triangles (scalene, isosceles, equilateral) and quadrilaterals (square, rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid). I can use geometric shapes to create complex designs and patterns. I can apply my knowledge of geometric shapes to solve real-world problems, such as measuring the area of a room or calculating the distance between two points.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. I can identify these shapes in two-dimensional figures.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can draw lines, line segments, and rays. I can identify right angles in shapes. I can identify parallel lines in pictures.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can draw simple shapes like squares and circles. I can identify some shapes like triangles and rectangles in pictures.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can distinguish between parallel and intersecting lines. I can use a road map rug, trace over the parallel lines and then trace over the intersecting lines. I can use a map of the school on an interactive whiteboard, trace the classrooms that are in a parallel line and the hallways that intersect. I can Find parallel lines in shapes.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can identify a line. I can use yarn, stretch and glue a line on paper. I can Draw a line when directed. I can walk on a line taped to the floor when directed. I can when given a line and a circle, indicate which is the line.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can identify an intersecting line. I can use sidewalk chalk to draw an intersecting line. I can go on an environment hunt and identify intersecting lines. I can Trace intersecting lines (e.g., roads or hallways) on a map.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Draw and identify lines and angles and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
text: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles as a category and identify right triangles.
ee_text: Describe the defining attributes of two-dimensional shapes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can classify and describe complex 2D figures, including those with multiple types of lines and angles. I can use my knowledge of angles and lines to solve problems, such as finding missing angle measures or determining if two figures are congruent. I can apply my understanding of right triangles to real-world situations, such as calculating the height of a building or the distance across a river. I can explain the relationship between right triangles and other geometric concepts, such as Pythagorean theorem and trigonometry. I can create my own 2D figures with specific properties, such as a quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides and four right angles (a rectangle).
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can classify any 2D figure based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size. I can explain the difference between parallel and perpendicular lines and identify them in complex figures. I can identify and measure angles using a protractor, including right angles and other specific angle sizes. I can recognize and identify right triangles based on their properties, including a right angle and two acute angles. I can explain why a triangle with a right angle is called a "right triangle."
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify most common 2D shapes, including triangles, squares, rectangles, and circles. I can identify parallel and perpendicular lines in simple figures. I can identify right angles in shapes and understand that they measure 90 degrees. I can recognize some right triangles, but I may not be able to explain why they are right triangles.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some shapes, like circles and squares, but I have difficulty identifying shapes with more sides or complex features. I can sometimes tell if lines are straight or curved, but I don't understand the difference between parallel and perpendicular lines. I can recognize some angles as "big" or "small," but I don't know the specific names for different angle sizes. I have seen triangles before, but I don't know what makes a triangle a "right triangle."

subject: Math
cluster: A. Draw and identify lines and angles and classify shapes by properties of their lines and angles.
text: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two- dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts. Identify line- symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
ee_text: Recognize that lines of symmetry partition shapes into equal areas.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify lines of symmetry for three-dimensional figures. I can also use my understanding of line symmetry to create symmetrical designs and patterns.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify a line of symmetry for any two-dimensional figure. I can also draw lines of symmetry for two-dimensional figures.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify a line of symmetry for some figures, but I still have trouble with others, especially if the figure has multiple lines of symmetry.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify a line that divides a figure in half, but I don't understand that the two halves need to be exactly the same.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can recognize a line of symmetry in a simple shape. I can place dots of paint on a coffee filter and fold in half. Place a pipe cleaner on the line of symmetry. I can use a symmetry mirror, move it around on shapes until the students see that both sides match.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can recognize simple shapes (square, triangle, and rectangle). I can Identify the shapes of environmental signs. I can Match the name to a shape from two choices.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can recognize polygons. I can when given a “mystery bag” with a geometric shape in it, find three objects, from around the school that match the shape and bring them back to class. Takes turns showing their items and have the rest of the students guess what the “mystery shape” is. I can identify polygons in pictures/shape.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Write and interpret numerical expressions.
text: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: Accurately solve complex, multi-step real-world problems by applying their knowledge of grouping symbols and order of operations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: Accurately evaluate numerical expressions with parentheses, brackets, or braces, demonstrating understanding of the order of operations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: Correctly evaluate numerical expressions containing parentheses alongside other operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division).
descriptors.cc_emerging: Solve simple addition and subtraction problems where the parentheses are provided and dictate the only steps to take. (Ex: 5 + (3 - 1) )

subject: Math
cluster: A. Write and interpret numerical expressions.
text: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. For example, express the calculation "add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" as 2 x (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 x (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create complex expressions that involve multiple operations and apply them to real-world scenarios. Example: I can write an expression to calculate the total cost of buying 3 pizzas at $12 each and 4 sodas at $2 each: (3 x $12) + (4 x $2) I can explain that this expression represents the cost of the pizzas plus the cost of the sodas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating themfrom a given real world scenario. Example: "Add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2" is written as 2 x (8 + 7). I can recognize that 3 x (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a simple expression with parentheses but may not understand the order of operations from a given scenerio. Example: "Add 4 and 2, then multiply by 5" is written as (4 + 2) x 5, but I may not understand that the addition must be done first.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a simple addition, subtraction, multiplication and/or division expression based on a given scenerio. Example: "Add 5 and 3" is written as 5 + 3.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Analyze patterns and relationships.
text: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify apparent relationships between corresponding terms. Form ordered pairs consisting of corresponding terms from the two patterns and graph the ordered pairs on a coordinate plane. For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, generate terms in the resulting sequences, and observe that the terms in one sequence are twice the corresponding terms in the other sequence. Explain informally why this is so.
ee_text: Identify and extend numerical patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply the concept of patterns and relationships to real-world scenarios and analyze data. For example, I can analyze the relationship between the number of hours worked and the amount of money earned, create a graph to represent this relationship, and use it to predict earnings for different work hours.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can generate two numerical patterns with given rules, identify the relationship between corresponding terms, form ordered pairs, and graph them on a coordinate plane. For example, given the rule "Add 3" and the starting number 0, and given the rule "Add 6" and the starting number 0, I can generate the first five terms in each sequence (0, 3, 6, 9, 12 and 0, 6, 12, 18, 24), identify that the second sequence is always twice the first, form ordered pairs (0,0), (3,6), (6,12), (9,18), (12,24), and graph them on a coordinate plane.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can generate two simple patterns with given rules and identify some corresponding terms. For example, I can find the first four terms in the pattern "Add 2" starting with 1 and the first four terms in the pattern "Add 4" starting with 1, and I can identify that the second pattern's numbers are always bigger than the first pattern's numbers.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify the first few terms in a pattern given a simple rule. For example, I can find the first three numbers in a pattern that starts with 2 and adds 5 each time. Ex. Show me a pattern that increases by two and starts at 0 (i.e., 0, 2, 4, 6,. . . ). Ex. Show me a pattern that increases by five and starts with 0 (i.e., 0, 5, 10, 15, . . . ).
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify and extend numerical patterns. I can Identify the following pattern as counting by twos and extend the pattern: 2, 4, 6, , , . I can Identify the following pattern as counting by tens and extend the pattern: 23, 33, 43, , .
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can repeat a pattern. I can Teacher claps twice, student claps twice. I can Activate a switch or indicate which choice shown repeats the pattern shown.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can extend a picture pattern. I can when given red, red, blue, red, red, , identify the missing color. I can Square, circle, triangle, square, , triangle. Identify the missing shape.

subject: Math
strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten
cluster: A. Understand the place value system.
text: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.
ee_text: Compare numbers up to 99 using place value models.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply the relationship between place values to solve real-world problems involving money and measurement. Ex: The student can explain that $4.50 is ten times greater than $0.45 and can use this understanding to solve problems like calculating the cost of ten items priced at $0.45 each. They can also apply this understanding to convert units of measurement, such as kilometers to meters or liters to milliliters.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the digit "4" in the number 400,000 represents 4 hundred thousands, which is ten times greater than the "4" in the number 40,000, which represents 4 ten thousands. Ex: The student can explain that the "4" in 400,000 represents 4 hundred thousands, which is ten times greater than the "4" in the number 40,000, which represents 4 ten thousands. They can also explain that the "4" in 40,000 is ten times greater than the "4" in 4,000, which represents 4 thousands.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain that the digit "4" in the number 4,567 represents 4 thousands, which is ten times greater than the "4" in the number 456, which represents 4 hundreds. Ex: The student can explain that the "4" in 4,567 represents 4 thousands, which is ten times greater than the "4" in the number 456, which represents 4 hundreds. They can also explain that the "4" in 456 is ten times greater than the "4" in 45.6.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can explain that a digit in the hundreds place is ten times greater than the same digit in the ten place. Ex: The student can explain that the "2" in the number 225 represents 2 hundreds, which is ten times greater than the "2" in the number 25 which represents 2 tens.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can compare numbers by composing and decomposing in two different ways. I can Decompose numbers by place value and compare by hundreds, tens, and ones (with the understanding that one 100, two 10s, and three ones combined is 123 ones). I can Compose numbers based on place value and compare to another number on the number line. I can Compare two numbers with different numbers in the tens place (e.g., 20 compared to 60 on the number line and explain 20 has two 10s or 20 ones and 60 is made of six 10s or 60 ones as it is written.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can compare numbers to 20. I can Using a number line and given two numbers, indicate where on the number line the numbers belong between the 10 markers. I can when given two numbers, indicate which one is greater, or less, or which comes first or last.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can compare numbers to each other based on place value groups by composing and decomposing to 99. I can Compare two numbers with different numbers in the tens place (e.g., 20 compared to 60 on the number line). I can Demonstrate the difference between two numbers using dimes (e.g., 10 compared to 50). I can Decompose a number into tens and ones, given two different numbers (with the understanding that two 10s and three ones combined is 23 ones). I can Compare numbers on a table of ones and tens, given two different numbers.

subject: Math
strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten
cluster: A. Understand the place value system.
text: Explain patterns in the number of zeros of the product when multiplying a number by powers of 10 and explain patterns in the placement of the decimal point when a decimal is multiplied or divided by a power of 10. Use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10.
ee_text: Use the number of zeros in numbers that are powers of 10 to determine which values are equal, greater than, or less than another number.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of multiplying and dividing decimals by powers of 10 to solve real-world problems, such as converting kilometers to meters or milligrams to grams. I can explain how the placement of the decimal point affects the units of measurement.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that multiplying a number by 10^n (where n is a whole number) shifts the decimal point n places to the right, and dividing by 10^n shifts the decimal point n places to the left. I can use whole-number exponents to represent powers of 10.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can correctly multiply a whole number by 10, 100, and 1000 and explain that the number of zeros in the product matches the number of zeros in the power of 10.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify that multiplying by 10 adds a zero to the end of a whole number because of the shift in the digits, but I struggle to explain why.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can look at the number of zeros in numbers like 10, 100, and 1,000 to decide which is greater, less, or equal to another number. I can compare numbers like 100 and 1,000 by counting the zeros and saying which one is larger or smaller.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can recognize when a number has one zero or more than one zero and understand that more zeros usually mean a bigger number with support. I can identify which number has more zeros when looking at two numbers, like 10 and 100, with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can look at numbers like 10 and 100 and use the zeros to help me say which number is greater with help. I can point to the number with more zeros to show it is bigger, or fewer zeros to show it is smaller, with guidance.

subject: Math
strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten
cluster: A. Understand the place value system.
text: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths. a. Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form, e.g., 347.392 = 3 x 100 + 4 x 10 + 7 x 1 + 3 x (1/10) + 9 x (1/100) + 2 x (1/1000).
ee_text: Compare whole numbers up to 100 using symbols (<, >, =).

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. descriptors.ee_emerging: I can identify the greater number between two single-digit numbers. I can use the terms "greater than" and "less than" to compare two small numbers
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can compare two-digit numbers using the symbols "<" and ">". I can correctly identify the greater number in a set of three numbers up to 100. I can use the equal sign (=) to show when two numbers are the same

subject: Math
strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten

subject: Math
strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten
cluster: B. Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.
text: Flexibly and efficiently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using strategies or algorithms based on place value, area models, and the properties of operations.
ee_text: Use the meaning of multiplication to develop and understand strategies to find products with multiples of 0, 1, 2, 5, and 10 within 100.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can multiply multi-digit numbers with decimals using the standard algorithm. I can use my understanding of multiplication to solve real-world problems, such as calculating the area of a rectangular garden or the cost of buying multiple items at the store. I can create my own strategies for multiplying multi-digit numbers, such as using mental math or a lattice method.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can multiply a two-digit number by a two-digit number using a standard algorithm based on place value and the distributive property. I can explain the steps of the algorithm and how they relate to place value and the distributive property. I can choose the most efficient strategy for multiplying two multi-digit numbers based on the numbers involved.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a place value table to multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number. I can use the distributive property to break apart a multiplication problem into easier parts. I can estimate the product of two multi-digit numbers.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can skip-count by 10s and 100s to find the product of a multi-digit number and a one-digit number. I can use repeated addition to find the product of a multi-digit number and a one-digit number.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use the meaning of multiplication to explain why the product of any number and 0 is 0. I can use the meaning of multiplication to explain why the product of any number and 1 is the number itself. I can use the commutative and associative properties of multiplication to find products more efficiently. I can use a variety of strategies to find the product of any number and a multiple of 0, 1, 2, 5, or 10 within 100. I can explain my thinking and reasoning when using different multiplication strategies.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can skip count by 2s, 5s, and 10s to find the product of a number and 2, 5, or 10. I can use repeated addition to find the product of a number and 0, 1, or 2.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can use the distributive property to break apart a multiplication problem into smaller, easier problems. For example, I can find the product of 3 x 6 by breaking it into (3 x 2) + (3 x 4). I can use multiplication facts I know to find other related facts. For example, if I know 5 x 5 = 25, I can use that to find 5 x 10 = 50. I can use manipulatives, such as counters or blocks, to represent multiplication problems and find the product.

source: CCEE Math Standards 2024 V1 Complete.xlsx (school)

subject: Math
strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten
cluster: B. Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.
text: Find whole-number quotients of whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division. Illustrate and explain the calculation by using equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
ee_text: Illustrate the concept of division using fair and equal shares.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use mental math strategies to estimate the quotient of large numbers. I can solve multi-step word problems involving division with large numbers. I can explain how division is used in real-world situations, such as calculating the cost per unit or the number of equal groups that can be formed from a given quantity.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use long division to find the quotient of a four-digit number and a two-digit number. I can explain my steps using equations, rectangular arrays, and area models. I can recognize and apply the relationship between multiplication and division to check my answer.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use partial quotients to find the quotient of a three-digit number and a two-digit number. I can explain my thinking using place value vocabulary.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use repeated subtraction to find the quotient of a two-digit number and a single-digit number. I can use repeated addition to find the produce of a two-digit number and a single-digit number. I can use pictures or manipulatives to represent the division problem. I can understand the inverse operation of multiplication and division of fact famlies.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can apply the concept of fair share and equal shares to solve a division problem. I can Divide a snack equally among classmates. I can Divide a square piece of paper equally among classmates. I can Divide themselves into equal teams. I can Divide a quantity into equal shares (e.g., “If I find 20 dollars, how could five people share this?” 20/5=4 (division structure partitive/fair shares).
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can construct equal sets. I can Using sorting tray and colored blocks to construct equal sets. I can when given 16 pencils, share equally onto four students. I can Use an organizer to group or partition objects into two or more sets. I can Create a model of equal sets by counting the objects in each set.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can illustrate the concept of division using fair and equal shares. I can Fold paper in equal shares. I can when given 10 counting cubes divided among three students, recognize when students have the same number (equal share) and when students do not have the same number (not equal share).

subject: Math
strand: Number and Operations in Base Ten
cluster: B. Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths.
text: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used. * Students are not required to rename fractions in lowest terms nor use least common denominators.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of decimals to solve real-world problems involving area, perimeter, volume, and other complex calculations. I can create my own strategies for adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing decimals based on my understanding of place value and properties of operations. I can explain my reasoning clearly and concisely, using mathematical vocabulary and notation. I can use technology, such as spreadsheets or calculators, to solve complex problems involving decimals..
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths using concrete models or drawings. I can explain my reasoning for choosing a specific strategy based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction. I can solve multi-step word problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of decimals with accuracy. I can relate the strategies I use with concrete models to written methods for solving problems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add and subtract decimals to the tenths place using a place value chart and manipulatives. I can explain the relationship between addition and subtraction of decimals using concrete examples. I can solve simple word problems involving addition and subtraction of decimals with some assistance.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can add and subtract whole numbers using manipulatives, but I struggle to apply this understanding to decimals. I can estimate the sum or difference of decimals, but I have difficulty using place value to solve problems accurately.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify all models of tenths, and I can explain how the parts relate to the whole. Example: I can identify that 7/10 is represented by 7 out of 10 equal parts of a whole, and I can explain that 7/10 is more than 5/10 but less than 8/10.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can identify some models of tenths, but I may need help counting or understanding the parts. Example: I can identify that a half is equal to 5/10, but I may not be able to explain why
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can identify most models of tenths, and I can explain how the parts relate to the whole. Example: I can identify that 3/10 is represented by 3 out of 10 equal parts of a whole, and I can explain that 3/10 is less than 5/10.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.
text: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers using flexible and efficient strategies, including renaming fractions with equivalent fractions. Justify using visual models (e.g., tape diagrams or number lines) and equations. For example, 2/3 + 5/4 = 8/12 + 15/12 = 23/12.
ee_text: Identify models of halves (½, 2/2), thirds (⅓, ⅔, 3/3), and fourths (¼, 2/4, ¾, 4/4).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers efficiently using mental math strategies. I can apply my understanding of adding and subtracting fractions to solve real-world problems, such as calculating the total amount of fabric needed for a project or figuring out how much time it takes to complete two tasks. I can explain my solutions using sophisticated vocabulary and complex sentences. I can also explain the reasoning behind my chosen strategies and connect them to other mathematical concepts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with different denominators by finding a common denominator and using equivalent fractions. I can justify my solutions using visual models (e.g., tape diagrams or number lines) and equations. I can explain my reasoning clearly and concisely.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add and subtract fractions with the same denominator by finding a common denominator. I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators using visual models like number lines, but I sometimes make mistakes when converting fractions to equivalent fractions. I can explain my reasoning using simple sentences.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can add and subtract fractions with the same denominator by counting the total number of parts in the numerator. I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators by drawing pictures, but I struggle to explain my reasoning.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify halves, thirds, and fourths of objects, even when the parts are not separated or labeled. I can identify different models representing the same fraction (e.g., recognizing that ½ of a circle and 2/4 of a rectangle represent the same amount). I can explain my reasoning for identifying the fractions of objects.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can identify a whole object and say it represents one. I can identify a half of an object and say it represents "half."
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can identify halves, thirds, and fourths of objects when the parts are clearly separated and labeled. I can match objects to their corresponding fraction models (e.g., matching a half of a pizza to a picture of ½).

subject: Math
cluster: A. Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions.
text: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem. Use benchmark fractions and number sense of fractions to estimate mentally and assess the reasonableness of answers. * For example, recognize an incorrect result 2/5 + 1/2 = 3/7, by observing that 3/7 <1/2.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers to solve real-world problems. For example, I can calculate the total amount of fabric needed to make two curtains, each requiring 2 1/2 yards of fabric. I can also explain my reasoning and justify my solutions using clear and concise language.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can add and subtract fractions with the same denominator by writing equivalent fractions with a common denominator. I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators by finding a common denominator using prime factorization.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators by finding a common denominator using prime factorization or using multiples without visual models
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can add and subtract fractions with the same denominator by counting the parts of a visual model I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators by finding a common denominator using multiples with visual models
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
text: Interpret a fraction as an equal sharing division situation, where a quantity (the numerator) is divided into equal parts (the denominator). Solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, by using visual fraction models (e.g., tape diagrams or area models) or equations to represent the problem. For example, when 3 wholes are shared equally among 4 people each person has a share of size 3/4. If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, how many pounds of rice should each person get? Between what two whole numbers does your answer lie?
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.6.RP.1.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of fractions and division to solve real-world problems involving equal sharing and interpret the results in context. Ex: I can calculate the amount of fabric needed to make 3 identical scarves if each scarf requires 2/3 yards of fabric. I can then determine the cost of the fabric based on its price per yard and apply my knowledge of fractions to calculate the total cost.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can interpret a fraction as an equal sharing division situation and solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers, using visual fraction models or equations. Ex: If 9 people want to share a 50-pound sack of rice equally by weight, each person should get 50/9 pounds of rice. This is a little more than 5 pounds (5 and 5/9 pounds) because 50 divided by 9 is 5 with a remainder of 5.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can divide a whole number into equal parts and represent the answer as a fraction, but I struggle to solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to answers in the form of fractions or mixed numbers. Ex: I can divide 5 pizzas into 8 equal slices and represent each slice as 5/8. However, I struggle to solve a word problem like "If 7 friends want to share 3 pizzas equally, how much pizza does each friend get?"
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can divide a whole number into equal parts but struggle to represent the answer as a fraction. Ex: Given 4 cookies to share equally among 3 friends, I can divide the cookies into 3 groups but cannot represent each friend's share as 4/3
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.6.RP.1.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
text: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction times a whole number (e.g., 2/3 x 4) or a fraction times a fraction (e.g., 2/3 x 4/5), including mixed numbers. a. Represent word problems involving multiplication of fractions using visual models to develop flexible and efficient strategies. For example, use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3, and create a story context for this equation. Do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. I can also apply this understanding to real-world situations, such as calculating the area of a garden plot with fractional dimensions or determining the amount of fabric needed for a project with fractional measurements.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can represent word problems involving multiplication of fractions using visual models to develop flexible and efficient strategies. For example, I can use a visual fraction model to show (2/3) × 4 = 8/3 and create a story context for this equation. I can also do the same with (2/3) × (4/5) = 8/15.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can multiply a whole number by a fraction with a visual model, but I struggle to create a story context for the equation.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use visual models (like fraction circles or drawings) to show what a fraction represents (e.g., showing 2/3 of a circle) and can identify the whole and the parts.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
text: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas of rectangles and represent fraction products as rectangular areas.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can calculate the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling with unit squares and explain why tiling gives the same result as multiplying the side lengths (e.g., "I tiled a rectangle with sides 1/2 and 2/3 using unit squares and showed the area equals 1/2 x 2/3"). I can represent products of fractions as areas and apply this understanding to solve real-world problems with rectangles of fractional side lengths.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling with unit squares and by multiplying the fractions (e.g., "I found the area of a rectangle with sides 3/4 and 2/5 by tiling it and confirmed it by multiplying 3/4 x 2/5"). I can explain how the product of two fractions represents the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the area of a simple rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling with unit fractions, with some guidance (e.g., "With help, I used unit squares to find the area of a rectangle with side lengths 1/2 and 1/3"). I can start to understand that multiplying fractional side lengths gives the area of a rectangle, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can begin to see that tiling a rectangle with fractional unit squares shows its area, with guidance (e.g., "With help, I used unit squares with side lengths 1/2 to cover a rectangle and find its area"). I can try using fractional units to cover a rectangle and start to understand how this relates to finding the area, with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
text: Interpret multiplication as scaling (resizing) by estimating whether a product will be larger or smaller than a given factor on the basis of the size of the other factor, without performing the indicated multiplication. a. Explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction greater than 1 results in a product greater than the given number and explain why multiplying a given number by a fraction less than 1 results in a product smaller than the given number.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply the concept of scaling to real-world situations and explain the effect of multiplying by fractions greater than or less than 1.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can estimate whether a product will be larger or smaller than a given factor based on the size of the other factor, without performing the multiplication.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes explain why multiplying by a fraction greater than 1 makes the product larger.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use pictures or objects to show that multiplying a whole number or fraction by a whole number makes something bigger or smaller.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
text: Relate the principle of fraction equivalence to the effect of multiplying or dividing a fraction by 1 or an equivalent form of 1 (e.g., 3/3, 5/5).
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why multiplying or dividing a fraction by an equivalent form of 1 (e.g., 4/4 or 6/6) does not change its value and use this principle to create equivalent fractions (e.g., "I multiplied 1/2 by 3/3 to make 3/6, which is the same value as 1/2"). I can apply the concept of fraction equivalence to simplify or scale fractions in real-world situations, explaining why the fraction remains unchanged.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can show that multiplying or dividing a fraction by an equivalent form of 1 (like 5/5 or 2/2) keeps the fraction equal in value (e.g., "I multiplied 2/3 by 2/2 to get 4/6, which is still equal to 2/3"). I can use this principle to create equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing by forms of 1.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can create simple equivalent fractions by multiplying by forms of 1, with some guidance (e.g., "With help, I multiplied 3/4 by 2/2 to make 6/8 and learned it is equal to 3/4"). I can start to understand that multiplying a fraction by an equivalent of 1 does not change its value, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can begin to understand that multiplying a fraction by a form of 1, like 3/3, keeps it the same, with guidance (e.g., "With help, I saw that 1/2 stays the same when I multiply by 2/2"). I can try to use simple examples to see that multiplying by forms of 1 keeps fractions equal, with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.N.CN.2b.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
text: Apply and extend previous understandings of division to divide unit fractions by whole numbers (e.g., 1/3 ÷ 4) and whole numbers by unit fractions (e.g., 4 ÷ 1/5). Students able to multiply fractions can develop strategies to divide fractions by reasoning about the relationship between multiplication and division. But division of a fraction by a fraction is not a requirement at this grade. a. Interpret and represent division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number as an equal sharing division situation. For example, create a story context for (1/3) ÷ 4, and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (1/3) ÷ 4 = 1/12 because (1/12) × 4 = 1/3.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.7.NS.2b.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create a real-world problem that involves dividing a unit fraction by a whole number or a whole number by a unit fraction. I can solve my problem, justify my solution using a visual model and an equation, and explain why my answer makes sense. Ex. Maria has 3 pizzas, and she wants to divide each pizza equally among her friends, giving each friend ⅙ of a whole pizza. How many friends can she share with?
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers by using visual fraction models and equations. For example, I can use a tape diagram to represent the problem "If a recipe calls for 1 1/2 cups of flour, and I want to make 2/3 of the recipe, how much flour do I need?" and write the equation 1 1/2 x 2/3 = 1.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a visual fraction model to solve a simple multiplication problem with fractions, but I may struggle to write the corresponding equation. For example, I can use a number line to find the product of 1/4 x 3, but I may not be able to write the equation 1/4 x 3 = 3/4.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify the correct visual model to represent a simple multiplication problem with fractions. For example, I can choose a tape diagram to represent 1/2 x 2.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.7.NS.2b.

source: CCEE Math Standards 2024 V1 Complete.xlsx (school)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.
text: Interpret and represent division of a whole number by a unit fraction as a measurement division situation. For example, create a story context for 4 ÷ (1/5), and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient. Use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of division of a whole number by a unit fraction to solve real-world problems. For example, I can use division to find out how many 1/5-cup servings of juice I can get from 4 cups of juice. I can explain my reasoning clearly and concisely using mathematical vocabulary. For example, I can explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because dividing 4 by 1/5 is the same as multiplying 4 by the reciprocal of 1/5, which is 5.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can interpret and represent division of a whole number by a unit fraction as a measurement division situation. For example, I can understand that 4 ÷ (1/5) represents dividing 4 objects into groups of 1/5 each, and that this is the same as finding out how many groups of 1/5 are in 4. I can use a visual fraction model to represent the division of a whole number by a unit fraction. For example, I can use a rectangular fraction model to show that 4 ÷ (1/5) is the same as dividing a rectangle with an area of 4 square units into 5 equal rows, and that the quotient is the number of rows. I can use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that 4 ÷ (1/5) = 20 because 20 × (1/5) = 4.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a visual model to show the division of a whole number by a unit fraction, recognizing that it represents partitioning the whole into groups of that unit fraction size. Example: Given 4 ÷ (1/5), I can draw a rectangle representing "4" and divide it into five equal parts to represent finding how many "fifths" are in the whole.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can demonstrate the meaning of dividing a whole number by a unit fraction using concrete objects or drawings, focusing on the idea of equal sharing. Ex: Given the problem 2 ÷ ½, the student can: Take two whole objects (e.g., cookies) and divide each cookie into halves. Count the total number of halves (4) to show the result of the division.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: CCEE Math Standards 2024 V1 Complete.xlsx (school)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can apply my understanding of dividing unit fractions and whole numbers to solve complex real-world problems. I can create my own word problems involving the division of unit fractions and whole numbers. I can explain the concept of dividing unit fractions and whole numbers to others. I can use my knowledge of dividing unit fractions and whole numbers in other areas of mathematics, such as algebra or geometry. I can solve problems like: Ex. A recipe calls for 2/3 cup of chopped nuts. If I only have 1/4 cup of chopped nuts, how many batches of the recipe can I make? Ex. A train travels 3/4 of a mile in 1/5 of an hour. What is the train's speed in miles per hour?
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use visual fraction models and equations to represent and solve real-world problems involving the division of unit fractions by non-zero whole numbers and the division of whole numbers by unit fractions. I can explain my reasoning using mathematical language. I can solve problems like: Ex. How much chocolate will each person get if 4 people share 1/3 lb. of chocolate equally? (Each person gets 1/12 lb. of chocolate.) Ex. How many 1/5-cup servings are in 4 cups of raisins? (There are 20 servings of size 1/5-cup of raisins.)
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can divide a unit fraction, like 1/2, into equal parts using a visual model. I can write a simple equation to represent the division of a unit fraction by a whole number, like 1/2 ÷ 3. I can solve simple real-world problems involving the division of a unit fraction by a whole number, like sharing 1/2 cup of flour equally among 3 friends.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can split a whole object, like a pizza, into equal parts. I can identify unit fractions, like halves, thirds, fourths, eighths.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.7.NS.2b.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system.
text: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m), and use these conversions in solving multi-step, real-world problems.
ee_text: Extend understanding of measurement concepts. a. Tell time using an analog or digital clock to the half or quarter hour. | Use standard units to measure weight and length of objects. | Indicate relative value of collections of coins.

descriptors.cc_advanced: Apply unit conversions to solve complex, real-world problems that involve multiple steps and multiple units. Explain the reasoning behind my conversions and calculations. Choose the most appropriate units for a given situation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: Convert fluently between different-sized standard units within the same measurement system (e.g., convert 5 cm to 0.05 m). Use these conversions to solve multi-step, real-world problems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: Use a ruler to measure length in inches and centimeters. Recognize that there are different units within the same measurement system (e.g., inches and feet are both units of length). Begin to make simple conversions between units within the same system (e.g., 12 inches = 1 foot). Ex: A student measures the length of a pencil in inches and then converts it to centimeters using a conversion chart. They can explain that there are 2.54 centimeters in 1 inch.
descriptors.cc_emerging: Count objects to measure length. Ex. Identify different units of measurement (e.g., inches, feet) but have difficulty relating them to each other.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell time using a digital clock to the minute and an analog clock to the nearest five minutes. I can tell time to the minute on a digital clock. I can place hand on a clock within five minutes of the stated time.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can tell time to the half-hour using a digital clock and to the half hour using an analog clock. I can identify which clock shows a stated time on a digital clock (3:30). I can Move hands on a clock to show a stated hour. | I can use a standard unit of measure, such as inches or centimeters, to measure the length of different objects accurately. I can use a standard unit of measure, such as pounds or kilograms, to measure the weight of different objects accurately.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can tell time using an analog or digital clock to quarter hour. I can indicate time to the quarter hour on a digital clock. I can place clock hands to show the half hour on an analog clock.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Represent and interpret data.
text: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Use operations on fractions for this grade to solve problems involving information presented in line plots. For example, given different measurements of liquid in identical beakers, find the amount of liquid each beaker would contain if the total amount in all the beakers were redistributed equally.
ee_text: Represent and interpret data on a picture graph, line plot, or bar graph.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create line plots that show data using fractions for more than one category. I can use my knowledge of fractions to solve real-world problems based on the information in the line plot and explain my thinking clearly. Ex: Students measure the length of different colored ribbons used in a craft project (red, blue, green) to the nearest ¼ inch. They create a line plot with color-coded Xs to display the length of each ribbon piece. They then answer questions like, "How much longer is the longest blue ribbon than the shortest red ribbon?" or "What is the total length of all the green ribbons used?"
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create a line plot to show measurements in fractions (like ½, ¼, ⅛). I can use addition, subtraction, and other fraction operations to answer questions about the data shown on the line plot and explain my thinking. Ex: Students measure the rainfall each day for a week to the nearest ¼ inch and record their data. They create a line plot to display the rainfall data. They then answer questions like, "How much more rain fell on Tuesday than on Thursday?" or "What was the total rainfall for the week?"
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can organize data in a tally chart and measure lengths to the nearest ¼ inch using a ruler. I can make a good guess about the value of a fraction on a number line. Ex: Students are given a collection of leaves and asked to measure the width of each leaf to the nearest ¼ inch. They record their measurements in a tally chart. They then practice placing fractions like ¾, ¼, and 1 ½ on a number line.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can draw a simple picture to represent data, count how many times something happens in the data, and name the different values in the data. Example: Students collect data on their classmates' favorite fruits (apple, banana, orange). They draw a picture to represent each fruit choice (e.g., a circle for each apple). They then count how many of each fruit picture they drew and name the different fruits in their data.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can collect, organize, and interpret data. Create a graph using a graph template, and display the data on the graph. I can count number of students who like dogs and number who like cats. Show where on the graph to put the bar for dogs and for cats and where to indicate the number of votes and enter the results on the graph. I can determine if the result shown seems reasonable and why (e.g., graph shows that students have more snakes as pets than dogs). I can based on class observation (how many wore red today), determine how to graph data and show graph telling which was more, less, or the same.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can display data on a picture, line plot, or bar graph and answer questions about the graph. I can indicate where data should go on the graph, and shade/color correct amount of spaces on given graph, answer a question about the graph (e.g., Is this about dogs?). I can use objects to display data on graph and indicate type of graph.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can represent and interpret data on a picture, line plot, or bar graph given a model and a graph to complete. I can when given data, plot data points on a given graph. Determine which has more, less, or the same. I can take given data from a survey and put the same data on a given graph using a model. Tell one thing the graph says about the survey.

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
text: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement. a. A cube with side length 1 unit, called a "unit cube", is said to have "one cubic unit" of volume, and can be used to measure volume.
ee_text: Identify common three- dimensional shapes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can calculate the volume of irregular solid figures by decomposing them into smaller shapes. I can apply my understanding of volume to solve real-world problems, such as determining the amount of water needed to fill a pool. I can explain the relationship between volume and density.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can calculate the volume of a rectangular prism by multiplying its length, width, and height. I can explain that the volume of a solid figure is measured in cubic units.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can measure the volume of a rectangular prism by counting the number of unit cubes it can hold. I can explain that the volume of a solid figure is the amount of space it occupies. I can recognize that a solid figure with a larger volume can hold more objects than a solid figure with a smaller volume.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify the volume of a cube with side length 1 unit as "one cubic unit." I can recognize that some solid figures can be filled with unit cubes.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can determine volume of a cube by counting units of measure. I can when given cubes that fill a box with no gaps (small number, how many), determine by counting the number of cubes needed to fill the box. I can when given a cube 4 x 4 x 4 inches constructed of one square inch cube, disassemble it to determine by counting how many cubes were required.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can demonstrate solid or liquid, full or empty. I can when given a glass of water and a paper weight, indicate which one you can pour. I can when given a glass of water and a paper weight, demonstrate that the water is liquid by pouring into another container. I can when given a glass full of water and an empty glass, indicate which one is full and which one is empty.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can identify objects that have volume. I can when given a group of pictures (cup, rock, fork), choose which one can be filled. I can identify objects in the room that can be filled (e.g., cup, fish tank). I can when given a square and a cube, indicate cube.

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
text: A solid figure which can be packed without gaps or overlaps using n unit cubes is said to have a volume of n cubic units.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why packing a solid figure completely with unit cubes gives its volume and use this principle to find and justify the volume of different shapes (e.g., "I packed a box with 24 unit cubes and explained that the volume is 24 cubic units because it’s fully filled"). I can use unit cubes to compare volumes of different shapes and explain how the number of cubes relates to the volume of each shape.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find the volume of a solid figure by counting the number of unit cubes that fit inside without gaps or overlaps (e.g., "I used 12 unit cubes to fill a rectangular prism, so the volume is 12 cubic units"). I can explain that the volume of a shape is the total number of unit cubes that fill it.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can determine the volume of a simple shape by counting the unit cubes that fill it, with some guidance (e.g., "With help, I counted 8 cubes in a small box to find that its volume is 8 cubic units"). I can start to understand that filling a shape with unit cubes gives the shape’s volume, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can begin to understand that filling a solid figure with unit cubes helps measure its volume, with guidance (e.g., "With support, I used cubes to see how many fit in a small box"). I can try counting unit cubes to find the volume of simple shapes, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
text: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes, using cubic cm, cubic in., cubic ft., and improvised units.
ee_text: Determine the volume of a rectangular prism by counting units of measure (unit cubes).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find the volume of a cylinder by using the formula: Volume = πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the height. I can use my knowledge of volume to solve real-world problems, such as calculating the amount of water needed to fill a pool or the amount of soil needed to fill a garden bed. I can explain the relationship between the volume of an object and its dimensions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by using the formula: Volume = Length x Width x Height. I can use cubic centimeters, cubic inches, and cubic feet to measure the volume of different objects. I can use improvised units to measure the volume of irregular objects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by counting the unit cubes needed to fill it. I can use cubic centimeters to measure the volume of a rectangular prism.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can determine the volume of a rectangular prism by counting unit cubes along all three edges. I can explain that the volume of a rectangular prism is the length x width x height. I can solve word problems involving the volume of rectangular prisms.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by counting unit cubes along edges. I can explain that the volume of a rectangular prism is the number of unit cubes that fit inside it.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can identify the faces of a rectangular prism. I can count the number of unit cubes along one edge of a rectangular prism.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can design and build different rectangular prisms with a specific volume using unit cubes. Example: A student is challenged to build as many different rectangular prisms as possible with a volume of 24 cubic units. They might build a 2 x 3 x 4 prism, a 1 x 6 x 4 prism, a 1 x 12 x 2 prism, etc. They can explain that volume is found by multiplying length x width x height or by recognizing layers within the prism.

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
text: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real- world and mathematical problems involving volume. a. Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths by packing it with unit cubes and show that the volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the edge lengths, equivalently by multiplying the height by the area of the base. Represent threefold whole-number products as volumes, e.g., to represent the associative property of multiplication.
ee_text: Determine the volume of a rectangular prism by counting units of measure (unit cubes).

descriptors.cc_advanced: Students will: I can explain the relationship between volume and the operations of multiplication and addition. I can use the concept of volume to solve complex real-world problems, such as calculating the amount of concrete needed to build a patio or the amount of water needed to fill a swimming pool. I can extend the concept of volume to other three-dimensional shapes, such as cylinders and cones. I can create my own formulas for finding the volume of different shapes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: Students will: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by packing it with unit cubes and multiplying the edge lengths. I can use the formula V = l x w x h to find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths. I can apply the formulas V = l x w x h and V = B x h to find the volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in real-world and mathematical problems. I can recognize volume as additive and find the volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts. I can solve real-world problems involving the volume of rectangular prisms.
descriptors.cc_approaching: Students will: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by counting unit cubes and multiplying the length, width, and height. I can explain that the volume of a rectangular prism is the same as the area of the base multiplied by the height. I can use the formula V = l x w x h to find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number side lengths.
descriptors.cc_emerging: Students will: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by counting the number of unit cubes that fit inside it. I can explain that the volume of a rectangular prism is the length x width x height. I can use the formula V = l x w x h to find the volume of a rectangular prism.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by counting the unit cubes in one layer and using that to figure out the total volume. Example: when given a rectangular prism (let's say 4 cubes long, 2 cubes wide, and 3 cubes high), the student can: Count the cubes in the bottom layer (8 cubes). Determine there are 3 layers in total. Calculate the total volume (8 cubes per layer x 3 layers = 24 cubic units).
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can identify the length, width, and height of a rectangular prism. I am starting to understand that the volume of a rectangular prism is related to the number of unit cubes that fit inside it.

source: CCEE Math Standards 2024 V1 Complete.xlsx (school)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
text: Apply the formulas V = l x w x h and V = B x h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole number edge lengths in the context of solving real- world and mathematical problems.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find the volume of rectangular prisms in complex real-world situations using the formulas 𝑉 = 𝑙 × 𝑤 × ℎ and 𝑉 = 𝐵 × ℎ V=B×h, and explain why both formulas give the same result (e.g., "I used both formulas to find the volume of a shipping box and confirmed they match"). I can solve multi-step volume problems involving rectangular prisms by applying the correct formula and justifying each step.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the formulas 𝑉 = 𝑙 × 𝑤 × ℎ and 𝑉 = 𝐵 × ℎ to find the volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edge lengths (e.g., "I calculated the volume of a box with length 4, width 3, and height 2 as 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 cubic units"). I can choose the appropriate formula and apply it correctly in mathematical and real-world volume problems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism by filling in values for length, width, and height in the formula 𝑉 = 𝑙 × 𝑤 × ℎ , with some guidance (e.g., "With help, I used the formula to find the volume of a prism with length 5, width 2, and height 3"). I can start to understand how the volume formula calculates the space inside a rectangular prism, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can begin to use the formula 𝑉 = 𝑙 × 𝑤 × ℎ to find the volume of simple prisms, with guidance (e.g., "With support, I used 3 x 2 x 1 to calculate the volume of a small box"). I can try substituting values in the volume formula to find the space inside a rectangular shape, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

subject: Math
cluster: C. Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition.
text: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of solid figures composed of two non-overlapping right rectangular prisms by adding the volumes of the non-overlapping parts, applying this technique to solve real- world problems.
ee_text: Not Applicable

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find the total volume of complex shapes by breaking them into two or more non-overlapping rectangular prisms, calculating each part, and adding the results (e.g., "I split a storage unit into two sections and found the total volume by adding each section's volume"). I can apply the additive volume property to solve real-world problems, explaining why adding the separate volumes gives the total.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find the volume of a figure made of two non-overlapping rectangular prisms by calculating each prism’s volume and adding them together (e.g., "I found the volume of a combined shape by adding the volumes of the two parts"). I can explain that adding the volumes of non-overlapping parts gives the total volume of the shape.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can start finding the volume of a figure made of two prisms by calculating each prism’s volume with help and adding them (e.g., "With guidance, I calculated the volume of each section and added them"). I can understand that combining volumes of separate parts gives a total volume, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can begin to understand that the volume of a figure with two parts can be found by adding each part's volume, with help (e.g., "With support, I found the volume of each part and added them to get the total"). I can try using simple volumes to see how separate parts add up to make a whole, with guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable
