subject: Math
cluster: C. Perform operations on matrices and use matrices in applications.
text: Work with 2 x 2 matrices as transformations of the plane and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use 2 × 2 matrices to transform shapes and explain how the determinant tells how the area changes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use 2 × 2 matrices as transformations of the plane and explain that the absolute value of the determinant is the area scale factor.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can multiply a 2 × 2 matrix by a point to transform it, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the area of a rectangle on a coordinate grid, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Interpret the structure of expressions.
text: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context. a. Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients. For example, in the expression representing height of a projective, -16t2+vt+c recognizing there are three terms in the expression, factors within some of the terms, and coefficients. Interpret within the context the meaning of the coefficient -16 as related to gravity, the factor of v as the initial velocity, and the c-term as initial height. b. Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity. For example, interpret the expression representing population growth P(1+r)n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P. Interpret the meaning of the P-factor as initial population and the other factor as being related to growth rate and a period of time.
ee_text: Identify an algebraic expression involving one arithmetic operation to represent a real-world problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can interpret complicated expressions by seeing parts as single objects and explain what each part means in context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can name the terms, factors and coefficients in an expression and explain what they mean in context. Example: in P(1 + r)ⁿ, P is the starting population.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the terms and coefficients of a simple expression with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify the numbers and operations in a simple expression and say what it means in words.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can choose an expression with one operation to represent a real-world problem.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Interpret the structure of expressions.
text: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it. For example, see x4-y4 as (x2)2-(y2)2, thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x 2-y2)(x2+y2).
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can see hidden structure in complex expressions and rewrite them in several ways, explaining which form is most useful.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the structure of an expression to rewrite it. Example: x^4 - y^4 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + y^2).
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can rewrite simple expressions, like a difference of squares, using a pattern with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find common factors in simple expressions with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Write expressions in ( equivalent forms to solve problems.
text: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression. a. Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines. b. Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines. c. Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions. For example, if the expression 1.15t represents growth in an investment account at time t (measured in years), it can be rewritten as (1.151/12)12t ≈ 1.01212t to reveal the approximate equivalent monthly rate of return is 1.2% based on an annual growth rate of 15%.
ee_text: Solve simple algebraic equations with one variable using multiplication and division.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the best form of an expression, factored, vertex or exponential, to answer a real-world question and explain what the form shows.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can factor quadratics to find zeros, complete the square to find a maximum or minimum, and rewrite exponential expressions. Example: x² - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3), zeros 2 and 3.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can factor simple quadratics with a leading coefficient of 1 and find the zeros with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find two numbers that multiply to one number and add to another, using a factor list.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can solve simple one-variable equations using multiplication and division.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Write expressions in ( equivalent forms to solve problems.
text: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculating mortgage payments or tracking the amount of an antibiotic in the human body when prescribed for an infection.
ee_text: Determine the successive term in a geometric sequence given the common ratio.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the geometric series formula to solve real problems, like loan payments, and explain what each part of the formula means.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (ratio not 1) and use it to solve problems.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the sum of a short geometric series by adding the terms, like 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 = 30, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the next term in a pattern that multiplies by the same number, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find the next term in a geometric sequence when I know the common ratio.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
cluster: A. Perform arithmetic operations on polynomials.
text: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why polynomials are closed under addition, subtraction and multiplication and compare this to integers.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can add, subtract and multiply polynomials. Example: (x + 2)(x + 3) = x² + 5x + 6.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add and subtract polynomials by combining like terms with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can combine like terms in simple expressions, such as 3x + 2x = 5x.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
cluster: B. Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.
text: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the Remainder Theorem to find factors and zeros of polynomials and explain why it works.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the Remainder Theorem: the remainder of p(x) divided by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 means x - a is a factor. Example: p(2) = 0 means x - 2 is a factor.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can evaluate p(a) and check if a value is a zero of a polynomial with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can substitute a number into a simple polynomial with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
cluster: B. Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials.
text: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find zeros of a polynomial, use them and end behavior to sketch its graph, and explain how multiplicity affects the graph.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find the zeros of a factored polynomial and use them to sketch a rough graph. Example: y = (x - 1)(x + 2) crosses the x-axis at 1 and -2.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the zeros of a polynomial that is already factored and mark them on the x-axis.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can solve simple equations like x - 3 = 0 and plot points on the x-axis.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
cluster: C. Use polynomial identities to solve problems.
text: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships. For example, use (a +20) =a2+40a+400 to mentally or efficiently square numbers in the 20s. (e.g., 2 222=22+2*40+400=484). Generalize to other double digit numbers. Use a2=(A+b)(a-b)+b2 and multiples of a*10 to square, e.g., 222=(22+12)(22-12)+122=340+144=484. Recognize the visual representation of (a+2b)2-a2=4ab as the area of a frame and find equivalent expressions.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can prove a polynomial identity and use it to explain a number pattern or calculate mentally, like squaring numbers in the 20s.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can prove polynomial identities and use them to describe number relationships. Example: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², so 22² = 400 + 80 + 4 = 484.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can expand a simple identity like (x + 2)² and check it with numbers, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the area of a square split into parts to show 12² = 100 + 40 + 4, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
cluster: C. Use polynomial identities to solve problems.
text: Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)n in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal’s Triangle.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the Binomial Theorem to find a specific term in an expansion without writing all the terms.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can expand (x + y)ⁿ using the Binomial Theorem and Pascal's Triangle. Example: (x + y)³ = x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can build Pascal's Triangle and use it to expand (x + y)² or (x + y)³ with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can multiply two binomials using the distributive property.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
cluster: D. Rewrite rational expressions.
text: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can rewrite complex rational expressions as q(x) + r(x)/b(x) and explain what each part shows about the expression.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can rewrite a(x)/b(x) as q(x) + r(x)/b(x) using inspection or long division. Example: (x^2 + 1)/(x - 1) = x + 1 + 2/(x - 1).
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can divide simple polynomials using long division steps with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can divide whole numbers and write the answer with a remainder as a fraction with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
cluster: D. Rewrite rational expressions.
text: Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide complex rational expressions, simplify fully, and explain why they behave like rational numbers.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide rational expressions and simplify the result. Example: 1/x + 2/x = 3/x.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add or multiply simple rational expressions with the same denominator using a worked example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide numerical fractions.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Create equations that ( describe numbers or relationships.
text: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
ee_text: Determine an equation involving at least one variable that can be used to solve a real-world problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create equations or inequalities for real problems, including quadratic or exponential situations, solve them and explain my answer.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create equations and inequalities in one variable from a problem and solve them. Example: 5 + 3x = 20, so x = 5.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write and solve a one-step or two-step linear equation from a word problem, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a bar model to find a missing number in a simple problem, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can write an equation with a variable that solves a real-world problem.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Create equations that ( describe numbers or relationships.
text: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
ee_text: Solve one-step inequalities.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create equations with two or more variables for real-world situations and use their graphs to answer questions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write equations in two variables for relationships and graph them with labeled axes and scales. Example: cost = 5 × tickets is y = 5x.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can graph a given two-variable equation on labeled axes using a table of values with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can plot points from a table on a coordinate plane.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can solve one-step inequalities.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Create equations that ( describe numbers or relationships.
text: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context. For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.
ee_text: Solve one-step inequalities.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write systems of equations or inequalities for real-world constraints, solve them, and explain which solutions are viable.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can represent constraints with equations, inequalities or systems and decide if solutions make sense in context. Example: 2x + 3y <= 20 for a budget of $20.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write one inequality for a simple constraint and test if a solution works with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use symbols like < and > to compare numbers in a situation with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can solve one-step inequalities.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Create equations that ( describe numbers or relationships.
text: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations. For example, rearrange the formula C = 5/9 (F-32) so you solve for F.
ee_text: Solve one-step inequalities.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can rearrange multi-step formulas from science or real life to solve for any variable and explain each step.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can rearrange a formula to solve for a chosen quantity, using the same steps as solving equations. Example: C = 5/9(F - 32) becomes F = 9/5C + 32.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can rearrange simple formulas like A = lw to solve for one variable with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can solve one-step equations using inverse operations.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can solve one-step inequalities.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.
text: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain and justify every step of solving an equation and argue why my method works.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain each step in solving a simple equation using properties of equality. Example: 2x + 3 = 11, subtract 3 to get 2x = 8, then divide by 2.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can solve a two-step equation and name the operation used in each step, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a balance model to show that both sides of an equation stay equal, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning.
text: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.CED.1.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can solve rational and radical equations and explain why some solutions are extraneous.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can solve simple rational and radical equations and check for extraneous solutions. Example: √x = x - 2 gives x = 4 (x = 1 is extraneous).
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can solve a simple radical equation by squaring both sides and checking my answer with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can solve one-step and two-step linear equations.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.CED.1.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.
text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.CED.1.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can solve multi-step linear equations and inequalities, including literal equations, and explain each step.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including ones with letter coefficients. Example: 3x - 5 > 7, so x > 4.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can solve two-step linear equations and inequalities with whole numbers with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can solve one-step equations with whole numbers with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.CED.1.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Solve equations and inequalities in one variable.
text: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x 2 = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula, factoring, and graphing as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the most efficient method to solve any quadratic equation, explain my choice, and write complex solutions as a ± bi.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can solve quadratic equations by square roots, factoring, completing the square, the quadratic formula or graphing. Example: x² = 49, so x = 7 or x = -7.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can solve quadratic equations by taking square roots or by using the quadratic formula with a step-by-step guide.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can solve simple equations like x² = 25 using a list of perfect squares.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Solve systems of equations.
text: Justify that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can prove that adding a multiple of one equation to another keeps the same solutions, and use this to solve systems.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can justify that replacing one equation with its sum with a multiple of the other gives a system with the same solutions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add two equations to remove a variable and check that the solution works in both, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can check if a pair of numbers makes two equations true, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Solve systems of equations.
text: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.REI.10.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write and solve systems of linear equations for real-world problems and explain what the solution means.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can solve systems of two linear equations exactly (algebra) and approximately (graphing). Example: y = x + 1 and y = 2x give x = 1, y = 2.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can solve a system of two linear equations by graphing or substitution with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can graph a linear equation and check if a point is a solution.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.REI.10.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Solve systems of equations.
text: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically. For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = -3x and the circle x2 + y2 = 3.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.REI.10.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can solve linear and quadratic systems in real-world problems and explain what the number of solutions means.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can solve a system of a linear and a quadratic equation by algebra and by graphing. Example: y = x and y = x^2 meet at (0, 0) and (1, 1).
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find where a line and a parabola meet by reading a graph with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can graph a line and find points on it with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.A.REI.10.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Solve systems of equations.
text: Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a system of linear equations as a matrix equation and explain how each part of the matrix equation matches the system.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write a system of linear equations as one matrix equation AX = B. Example: 2x + y = 5 and x - y = 1 becomes [2 1; 1 -1][x; y] = [5; 1].
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can pick out the coefficients and constants of a system and place them in a matrix with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify the coefficient and constant in a linear equation.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Solve systems of equations.
text: Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use inverse matrices and technology to solve real-world systems with 3 or more variables, and explain when an inverse exists.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations, using technology for 3 × 3 or larger.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix using a formula, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a system of two equations as a matrix, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: D. Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.
text: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).
ee_text: Interpret the meaning of a point on the graph of a line. For example, on a graph of pizza purchases, trace the graph to a point and tell the number of pizzas purchased and the total cost of the pizzas.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why each point on a graph is a solution and use the graph to answer real-world questions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that the graph of an equation in two variables shows all its solutions. Example: (2, 5) is on y = 2x + 1 because 5 = 2(2) + 1.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can check if a point is on the graph of a line by substituting into the equation with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can plot points on a coordinate plane and read the coordinates of a point.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can explain what a point on the graph of a line means, such as the number of pizzas and the total cost.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: D. Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.
text: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations.
ee_text: Interpret the meaning of a point on the graph of a line. For example, on a graph of pizza purchases, trace the graph to a point and tell the number of pizzas purchased and the total cost of the pizzas.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why intersection points solve f(x) = g(x) and use technology or tables to solve real-world problems.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that x-values where y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect solve f(x) = g(x), and find them with graphs, tables or approximations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find where two graphs cross using technology or a table with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read the coordinates of a point on a graph with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find and explain the meaning of a point on the graph of a line, like the number of pizzas and the total cost.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: D. Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically.
text: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality) and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.
ee_text: Interpret the meaning of a point on the graph of a line. For example, on a graph of pizza purchases, trace the graph to a point and tell the number of pizzas purchased and the total cost of the pizzas.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can graph a system of linear inequalities for a real-world problem and explain which points in the solution region make sense.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can graph the solutions of a linear inequality as a half-plane, using a dashed line for < or >, and find where two half-planes overlap. Example: y > x + 1 has a dashed line and shading above.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can graph the boundary line of an inequality and shade the correct side by testing a point with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can graph a linear equation from a table of values.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can explain what a point on the graph of a line means, such as the number of pizzas bought and their total cost.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.
text: Understand that a function from one set, discrete or continuous, (called the domain) to another set (called the range) assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range.
ee_text: Use the concept of function to solve problems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can decide if a relation is a function using mappings, tables or graphs, and explain using domain and range.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that a function assigns each element of the domain exactly one element of the range.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if a mapping diagram or table is a function, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match each input to its output using a simple rule, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use what a function is to solve problems.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.
text: Use function notation, evaluate functions. and interpret statements that use function notation in terms of a context.
ee_text: Use the concept of function to solve problems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use function notation to solve real-world problems and explain what statements like f(3) = 10 mean in context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use function notation, evaluate functions and explain function statements in context. Example: if f(x) = 2x + 1, then f(3) = 7.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can evaluate a function for a given input using function notation with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the output of an input/output table or rule for a given input.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use the idea of a function (input and output) to solve problems.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Understand the concept of a function and use function notation.
text: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of the integers. For example, in an arithmetic sequence, f(x) = f(x-1) + C or in a geometric sequence, f(x) = f(x-1) * C, where C is a constant.
ee_text: Use the concept of function to solve problems.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write recursive rules for sequences in real contexts and explain why a sequence is a function.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of context.
text: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities and sketch graphs showing key features given a verbal description of the relationship. Key features include: intercepts; intervals where the function is increasing, decreasing, positive, or negative; relative maximums and minimums; symmetries; end behavior; and periodicity.
ee_text: Construct graphs that represent linear functions with different rates of change and interpret the graphs. For example, which rate is faster/slower or higher/lower.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can sketch a graph from a description of a real-world relationship and explain how its key features match the situation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can interpret key features of graphs and tables, such as intercepts, increasing or decreasing intervals, maximums, minimums, symmetry and end behavior, in terms of the situation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify intercepts and where a graph is increasing or decreasing using a labeled graph and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read values from a graph and say whether it goes up or down with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can graph linear functions with different rates of change and explain which rate is faster or slower.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of context.
text: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and find an appropriate domain (discrete or continuous) in the context of the given problem.
ee_text: Construct graphs that represent linear functions with different rates of change and interpret the graphs. For example, which rate is faster/slower or higher/lower.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose a sensible domain for a function in a real problem and explain whether it should be discrete or continuous.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can relate a function's domain to its graph and find a suitable domain for the problem. Example: the number of tickets sold uses whole numbers only.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read the domain from a graph, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the input values shown on a simple graph or table, with help.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of context.
text: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a linear or nonlinear function (presented symbolically or as a table) over a specified interval. Estimate the rate of change from a graph.
ee_text: Construct graphs that represent linear functions with different rates of change and interpret the graphs. For example, which rate is faster/slower or higher/lower.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare average rates of change of different functions over intervals and explain what they mean in a real-world context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can calculate and explain the average rate of change of a function over an interval from an equation, table or graph. Example: from (1, 3) to (4, 12), rate = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the rate of change between two points in a table or graph with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find how much a quantity changes between two values in a table.

subject: Math
cluster: C. Analyze functions using different representations.
text: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph using an efficient method. a. Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima, and exponential functions, showing intercepts and end behavior. b. Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step functions and absolute value functions. c. Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros when suitable factorizations are available and showing end behavior. d. Graph rational functions, identifying zeros and asymptotes when suitable factorizations are available and showing end behavior. e. Graph logarithmic functions, showing intercepts and end behavior, and trigonometric functions, showing period, midline, and amplitude.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose an efficient method to graph any function type and explain what its key features, like zeros, asymptotes or period, mean in context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can graph linear, quadratic, exponential, root, piecewise, polynomial, rational, logarithmic and trigonometric functions and show key features like intercepts, maxima, minima, asymptotes and end behavior. Example: y = x^2 - 4 has a minimum at (0, -4).
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts and the maximum or minimum, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can plot points from a table on a coordinate grid with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.F.IF.1.

subject: Math
cluster: C. Analyze functions using different representations.
text: Write a function defined by an expression in equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties of the function. a. Use an efficient process to rewrite f(x) = ax2+bx+c as f(x) = a(x-h)2 +k or f(x)=a(x-p)(x-q) to determine the characteristics of the function and interpret these in terms of a context. b. Use the properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions. For example, identify percent rate of change in functions, where t is in years, such as y = (1.01)12t is approximately y = (1.127)t , where t is in years, meaning it is a 1% growth rate each month and a 12.7% growth rate each year. Identify percent rate of change in functions, where t is in years, such as y = (1.2)(t/10) is approximately y = (1.018)t , meaning it is a 20% growth rate each decade and a 1.8% growth rate each year.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can rewrite quadratic and exponential functions in different forms and explain what each form shows about a real-world situation.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can rewrite quadratics in vertex or factored form to find key features, and rewrite exponential functions to find percent rates of change. Example: y = 1.2^(t/10) means 20% growth each decade.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the zeros or vertex of a quadratic from a given form and identify growth or decay in an exponential function with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can factor simple quadratics and tell if a number above or below 1 means growth or decay.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Analyze functions using different representations.
text: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions). For example, given a graph of one quadratic function and an algebraic expression for another, say which has the larger maximum.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare two functions shown in different ways and explain which has a bigger maximum, rate of change or intercept, and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare properties of two functions shown in different ways, like a graph and an equation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compare one feature, like the y-intercept, of two functions shown in different ways, with support.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.
text: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities. a. Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context. b. Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations. For example: The temperature of a cup of coffee can be modeled by combining together a function representing difference in temperature and the actual room temperature, which results in an exponential model. An average cost function can be created by dividing the cost of purchasing n items by the number of n items purchased, which results in a rational function. c. Work with composition of functions using tables, graphs, and symbols. For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.
ee_text: Select a graph from the first quadrant of the coordinate plane that represents a situation involving constant rate of change. c. Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build functions by combining or composing functions to model real-world situations and explain what each part means.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write a function for a relationship using an expression or recursive rule, combine functions, and compose functions. Example: start at 10 and add 3 each step: f(n) = 10 + 3n.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a function rule from a table or simple context with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe a pattern in a table and continue it.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can choose a first-quadrant graph that shows a situation with a constant rate of change.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities.
text: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and with an explicit formula, use them to model situations, and translate between the two forms.
ee_text: Determine an arithmetic sequence with whole numbers when provided a recursive rule.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can model real situations with arithmetic and geometric sequences and explain when to use the recursive or explicit form.

descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the common difference in a simple pattern with help.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Build new functions from existing functions.
text: Identify the effect on the graph of replacing f(x) by f(x) + k, k f(x), f(kx), and f(x + k) using transformations for specific values of k (both positive and negative); find the value of k given the graphs. descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use technology to see how adding a number shifts a graph up, down, left or right with support.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Build new functions from existing functions.
text: Identify and create inverse functions, using tables, graphs, and symbolic methods to solve for the other variable. For example: Each car in a state is assigned a unique license plate number, and each license plate number is assigned to a unique car; thus there is an inverse relationship. Rearrange the formula C=59(F-32) so you solve for F. You examine a table of values and realize the inputs and outputs are invertible. Two graphs are symmetrical about the line y = x.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can undo a simple operation, like adding 3 is undone by subtracting 3, with help.

subject: Math

text: Understand the inverse relationship between exponents and logarithms and use this relationship to solve problems involving logarithms and exponents.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems.
text: Distinguish between situations that can be modeled with linear functions and with exponential functions. a. Prove that linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals and that exponential functions grow by equal factors over equal intervals. b. Recognize situations in which one quantity changes at a constant rate per unit interval relative to another. c. descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the volume of a rectangular prism with help.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Visualize relationships between twodimensional and three-dimensional objects.
text: Identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify the 3D object made when a 2D shape is rotated around a line. Example: Rotating a rectangle around one side makes a cylinder.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can match a 2D shape to the 3D object it makes when rotated, using pictures or models.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name common 2D and 3D shapes with support.

cluster: C. Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use geometric shapes, their measures and properties to describe real objects. Example: a can is like a cylinder.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the shape that best matches a real object, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match real objects to 3D shapes, like a ball to a sphere, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use the properties of shapes to describe real-life objects.

subject: Math
cluster: C. Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use density based on area or volume to solve problems. Example: 600 people in 3 square miles is 200 people per square mile.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find density by dividing an amount by area or volume with support.

subject: Math
cluster: C. Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations.
text: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios).
ee_text: Use properties of geometric shapes to describe real life objects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design an object that meets several constraints, such as lowest cost, and justify my design with geometric reasoning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use geometric methods to solve design problems, like designing a box that holds a set volume.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can solve a design problem with one constraint using a model or template with support.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.
text: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).
ee_text: Given data, construct a graph (line, pie, bar, or picture) or table and interpret the data.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can display data on a number line using dot plots, histograms and box plots.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can make a dot plot or histogram from a small data set using a given scale.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.
text: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.
ee_text: Given data, construct a graph (line, pie, bar, or picture) or table and interpret the data.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the right statistics for each data shape, compare two or more data sets, and explain my choice.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the right center (mean or median) and spread (IQR or standard deviation) for the data shape to compare data sets.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the middle value of a small ordered data set, with help.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.
text: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).
ee_text: Interpret trends on a graph or chart.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare data sets using shape, center and spread and explain how outliers change my conclusions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain differences in shape, center and spread of data sets in context and how outliers affect them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the center and spread of two data sets and identify an outlier with support.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable.
text: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use statistical packages calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.
ee_text: Calculate the mean of a given data set.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can decide when a normal model fits data, explain why, and use it to estimate population percentages in context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the mean and standard deviation to fit data to a normal distribution and estimate percentages with technology or tables. Example: about 68% lies within 1 standard deviation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use the mean and standard deviation with the 68-95-99.7 rule to estimate percentages with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the mean of a small data set with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can calculate the mean of a data set.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.
text: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies as examples of proportionality and disproportionality). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.F.IF.1.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use relative frequencies in a two-way table to describe associations in data and explain whether they suggest a trend.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can make a two-way frequency table, find joint, marginal and conditional relative frequencies, and describe possible associations. Example: 18 of 30 girls chose soccer, so 60%.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can complete a two-way table and find the totals for each row and column with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort data into categories and count each group.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.F.IF.1.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Summarize, represent, and interpret data on two categorical and quantitative variables.
text: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot and describe how the variables are related. a. Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data. Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize appropriate families of functions to model. b. Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals. c. Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can fit a function to scatter plot data, check its fit using residuals, and use it to solve problems in context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can show two-variable data on a scatter plot, fit a function to it and use it to solve problems, including fitting a linear function.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can make a scatter plot and draw a line of best fit, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can plot ordered pairs on a coordinate grid, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Interpret linear models
text: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.F.IF.4.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the slope and intercept of a linear model to make predictions and judge if they make sense in context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain the meaning of the slope and intercept of a linear model in context. Example: in cost = 2x + 5, $5 is the starting fee and $2 is cost per item.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the slope and intercept of a linear model with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the slope of a line from a graph or two points.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable. See M.EE.F.IF.4.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Interpret linear models
text: Use technology to create a correlation coefficient for a linear fit and then interpret its meaning for the model.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use the correlation coefficient to compare linear models and explain the strength and direction of each in context.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use technology to find the correlation coefficient for a linear fit and explain what it means. Example: r = 0.9 shows a strong positive linear relationship.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if a correlation coefficient shows a strong or weak, positive or negative relationship with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe a scatter plot as going up or down with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: C. Interpret linear models
text: Distinguish between correlation and causation. For example, cities with a higher number of fast food restaurants tend to have more hospitals. While there is a clear correlation (likely driven by population), we cannot conclude that fast food restaurants are causing more hospitals to open. There is a relationship between height and reading level in elementary school children. This is not because changes in height cause better reading ability. Rather as children get older, they get both taller and improve in their reading skills.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain why a correlation does not prove causation and suggest another factor that could explain a relationship.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can tell the difference between correlation and causation. Example: Taller children read better, but height does not cause reading ability. Age affects both.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say whether two things are related in a data set and decide if one causes the other with sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can describe whether two quantities go up together using a picture or graph with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.
text: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.
ee_text: Determine the probability of an event occurring when the outcomes are equally likely to occur.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how a random sample is used to make an inference about a population and why a sample's results may differ.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain that statistics is a process for making inferences about a population from a random sample.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell the difference between a population and a sample, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can collect data from a small group and describe it, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find the probability of an event when all outcomes are equally likely.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Understand and evaluate random processes underlying statistical experiments.
text: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process (e.g., using simulation). For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?
ee_text: Determine the probability of an event occurring when the outcomes are equally likely to occur.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a simulation to test a model and explain whether the results give strong evidence against it.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can decide if a model fits results from a data-generating process using simulation. Example: 5 tails in a row has probability 1/32, which is unlikely but possible.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can run a simple simulation and compare the results to a model with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the probability of a simple event, such as getting heads on a coin.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find the probability of an event when all outcomes are equally likely.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

cluster: B. Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.
text: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.

text: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.

subject: Math
cluster: B. Make inferences and justify conclusions from sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies.
text: Evaluate reports based on data.
ee_text: Not applicable. See M.EE.SP.ID.1.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can critique a data report by checking its sampling, data and conclusions and suggest improvements.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate reports based on data by checking how the data was collected and if the conclusions are supported.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the claim and the data in a report and say if they match with support.

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: A. Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.
text: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").
ee_text: Identify when events are independent or dependent.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can describe complex events using unions, intersections and complements and explain them with Venn diagrams in real contexts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe events as subsets of a sample space and use "and", "or" and "not". Example: rolling an even number is {2, 4, 6}.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list the sample space and describe simple events using a diagram with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can list all the possible outcomes of a coin or a die with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify when events are independent or dependent.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: A. Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.
text: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.
ee_text: Identify when events are independent or dependent.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use probabilities from real-world data to decide if two events are independent and explain my reasoning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can decide if events A and B are independent by checking if P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B). Example: A coin and a die: P(heads and 6) = 1/2 × 1/6 = 1/12.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can multiply probabilities of two independent events, like coin flips, using a tree diagram or table.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the probability of a simple event, such as rolling a 3, as a fraction.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify when events are independent or dependent.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: A. Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.
text: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B) and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.
ee_text: Identify when events are independent or dependent.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use conditional probability to decide if two events are independent in a real situation and explain my reasoning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find P(A given B) as P(A and B)/P(B) and explain that A and B are independent when P(A given B) = P(A).
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find a conditional probability from a two-way table, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find a simple probability from a table, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell when two events are independent or dependent.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: A. Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.
text: Represent data from two categorical variables using two-way frequency tables or Venn diagrams. Interpret the representation when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the representation as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.
ee_text: Identify when events are independent or dependent.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can collect my own two-category data, make a two-way table, and use it to test independence and estimate conditional probabilities.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can make two-way tables or Venn diagrams for two categories and use them to decide if events are independent and estimate conditional probabilities.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read a two-way table and find a simple probability with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort data into categories using a table or Venn diagram.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify when events are independent or dependent.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: A. Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data.
text: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations. For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.
ee_text: Identify when events are independent or dependent.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare conditional probabilities in real situations and explain why P(A given B) is not the same as P(B given A).
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if two everyday events are independent or dependent using examples with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can explain if one event changes the chance of another in a simple situation with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify when events are independent or dependent.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: B. Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.
text: Use a representation such as a two-way table or Venn diagram to find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B’s outcomes that also belong to A and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find conditional probabilities from two-way tables or Venn diagrams in real-world contexts and explain what they mean.

descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find a conditional probability from a two-way table when the correct row or column is highlighted.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read counts from a two-way table or Venn diagram with support.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: B. Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model.
text: Use a representation such as a two-way table or Venn diagram to apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.

descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use a two-way table or Venn diagram to apply P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) and explain the answer.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find P(A or B) from a Venn diagram by counting, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort objects into a Venn diagram, with help.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

strand: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

cluster: A. Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.

subject: Math
cluster: A. Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.
text: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value. For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a probability distribution and use expected value to compare different grading schemes or choices.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can make a probability distribution for a random variable and find its expected value. Example: E = 0(0.5) + 10(0.5) = 5.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list the values and probabilities of a random variable in a table with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find theoretical probabilities when outcomes are equally likely.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: A. Calculate expected values and use them to solve problems.
text: Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value. For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can build a probability distribution from real data, find the expected value, and use it to make and explain predictions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can make a probability distribution from data and find the expected value. Example: if the expected value is 2.5 TVs, 100 homes have about 250 TVs.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find probabilities from a data table and compute an expected value with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the probability of an outcome from a simple table with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.
text: Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values. a. Find the expected payoff for a game of chance. For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast-food restaurant. b. Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values. For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare decisions or strategies, such as insurance plans, using expected values and explain which choice is better and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find the expected value of a game or decision by multiplying each payoff by its probability and adding. Example: Win $10 with 1/5 chance, else $0: expected value = $2.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the expected value of a simple game when the payoffs and probabilities are given in a table.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the probability of simple events and multiply a fraction by a whole number.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.
text: Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing for a party door prize where attendees earn one entry to the drawing for each activity they complete, using an electronic spinner to pick a team spokesperson at random from a group, flip a coin to decide which of two friends gets to choose the movie, using a random number generator to select people to include in a sample for an experiment).
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design a fair way to make a decision using probability and explain why it is fair.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use probabilities to make fair decisions, like flipping a coin or using a random number generator.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if a simple method, like a coin flip, is fair, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say if each person has the same chance in a simple game, with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.

source: Wisconsin Standards for Mathematics (2021); Wisconsin Essential Elements for Mathematics (2022)

subject: Math
cluster: B. Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions.
text: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., balancing expected gains and risk, medical product testing, choosing an investment option, deciding when to kick an extra point vs. two point conversion after a touchdown in football).
ee_text: Not applicable.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use probability and expected value to compare strategies in a real-world decision and justify the best choice.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use probability concepts, such as expected value, to analyze decisions and strategies.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find and compare the probability of two choices with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the probability of a simple event and say which choice is more likely.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable.
